chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had two men dispute before him over a beast of burden, and both presented evidence that they had given birth to it (acquired it by finding/producing it), so he ruled in its favor for the one who had it in his possession, and he said, 'If it had not been in his possession, I would have divided it between them into two halves.'

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤَمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (referring to Imam Ali)
key_terms.أَنْتَجَهَا: produced it / acquired it (by finding or generating)
key_terms.اِخْتَصَمَ: disputed / brought a case for adjudication

ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence determine ownership when two parties present equal evidence of acquisition?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam Ali (AS), the principle of *al-yamin* (possession) prevails when two parties present equal evidence, reflecting the Shia legal maxim that possession serves as a strong indicator of ownership. The Imam’s conditional statement highlights the pragmatic application of equity, ensuring that in the absence of physical control, justice is served through equal division, a concept deeply rooted in the Quranic emphasis on fair adjudication and the preservation of rights.
